Prize category: BEST USE OF THEME

Not every game needs a theme, and when used the theme need not be overpowering. But many players find games particularly satisfying when they have an unusual and immersive theme, with gameplay mechanics that flow from the theme. These games are the entertainment equivalent of fighting for a cause you believe in, rather than fighting just to fight.

Prize category: BEST RULE BOOK

Writing rules is a skill all on its own, and is essential for the success of a game. How well can players learn the game without you explaining it?

To place well in this category, you are encouraged to conduct blind playtests of your game. Watch someone read the rules then play your game. Take notes and use the insights to write a better rulebook.

You are strongly encouraged to review and give feedback on other designer's rulebooks, even if you end up not playing their game.

Prize category: BEST MULTI-PLAYER GAME

One of the challenges of a good multi-player design is to elevate the game out of the components and into the minds of the players. The rules must set bounds but allow the freedom for players to explore options such as predicting each other's behaviours, bluffing, recognizing weakness in the opponent's strategy, creating innovative solutions to dangerous situations - the thrust and parry of engaged minds.

Prize category: BEST GAME ON THIS YEAR'S THEME: LOGISTICS


Quote:
Battles are won by soldiers, wars are won by logistics.
Quote:
For want of a nail the shoe was lost.
For want of a shoe the horse was lost.
For want of a horse the rider was lost.
For want of a rider the battle was lost.
For want of a battle the kingdom was lost.
And all for the want of a horseshoe nail.
Wars require infrastructure for materiel, personnel and communications to manage them.

This category is for games depicting the importance of logistics management:

 Supply routes keeping fighting units in good shape (example: convoys delivering artillery shells while being protected from crippling ambushes)
 Rotating personnel who need rest and recuperation (example: assigning medical supplies to different outposts to heal injured soldiers. Weighing pushing tired soldiers into battle vs retreating)
 Communication (example: assigning combat ordres to a unit knowing their radios may be knocked out, preventing new orders from being sent later)

All games are automatically entered into this prize category.
